items.text: The White House announced the first three-way meeting of [[p:Donald Trump]], [[p:Xi Jinping]] and [[p:Vladimir Putin]], set for 19 Nov in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the [[p:Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation|APEC]] {{note: Pacific Rim economic forum founded in 1989 in Canberra on an Australian proposal.}} summit. Officials say Trump will raise cutting nuclear arsenals and the Iran war, but not Ukraine, which runs on a separate track. That contradicts Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov, who said Ukraine would be discussed. Trump also has a bilateral meeting with Xi, but no one-on-one with Putin.

[[p:Steve Witkoff]] and [[p:Jared Kushner]] briefed [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] in Dublin after seeing Putin. Zelenskyy said the agreed prisoner swap will be the largest of the war and that Europeans will join the next trilateral round; Kushner said no deal is possible without Europe at the table. Putin proposed a humanitarian mission in Kostiantynivka modelled on Oleshky; Kyiv says details need clarifying. No date or venue for the next round, and the Kremlin offered no concessions.

Militants ambushed police returning from a raid on illegal gold miners in Kohat, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. Officials say the hours-long gunfight killed 10 police officers and 18 militants. The [[p:Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan|Pakistani Taliban (TTP)]] {{note: Militant alliance formed in 2007 in the tribal areas under Baitullah Mehsud.}} claimed the attack; officials allege it colluded with criminal gangs.

Pakistan says it foiled a TTP infiltration attempt in the Shalozan sector of Kurram. Security sources say [[p:Taliban]] forces fired first and that Pakistani heavy weapons damaged Taliban border posts; on 6 Nov Pakistan reported capturing an Afghan national carrying a weapon and bomb-making notes. Kabul has not commented.
items.notes: Pakistani security-source claims; no independent confirmation.

items.text: The military's media wing ISPR says security forces killed 74 militants in intelligence-based operations in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan, 35 of them in Mir Ali.
items.notes: Military claim; figures not independently verifiable.

items.text: Jailed former PM [[p:Imran Khan]] was taken overnight to a hospital in Islamabad for an eye check-up and blood-pressure treatment, then returned to Adiala jail, officials told reporters. On 11 Nov his lawyers met him for several hours under an Islamabad High Court order; lawyer Latif Khosa said his blood pressure was at a frightening level and that a possible 28th constitutional amendment was discussed. [[p:Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf|PTI]] deputy chief [[p:Shah Mehmood Qureshi]] was also hospitalised in Lahore.
The Islamabad High Court suspended the schedule for Islamabad's local elections until a 26 Nov hearing on a challenge to constituency boundaries.

Russian Deputy PM Alexei Overchuk led a delegation of more than 70 businesspeople to Kabul, meeting Taliban PM Mohammad Hasan Akhund and deputy PM [[p:Abdul Ghani Baradar]], who invited Russian investment in mining, factories and railways. Overchuk said trade more than doubled to over $349m in the first eight months of 2026. No agreements were announced. Russia is the only country to have recognised the Taliban government.
Amu TV reports that about 500 families in the Omid-e Sabz township in western Kabul have been ordered to vacate their homes.
[[p:Amnesty International]] launched a global campaign urging recognition of gender apartheid in Taliban-ruled Afghanistan.

India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October, a two-year high and above the [[p:Reserve Bank of India]]'s 6% upper tolerance limit, from 5.5% in September. Food inflation reached 8.94%. Economists say the breach makes rate cuts less likely; analysts flag El Niño as a risk to food prices.

Nepal's opposition parties are closing ranks against PM [[p:Balen Shah]]. They demand a parliamentary session and want the PM, home minister and police chief questioned by a committee over the Inam Sapkota middleman case, which involves the PM's office. A [[p:Nepali Congress]] leader alleges the PM's chief adviser altered messages on a detainee's phone; the claim is unverified. Ruling-party chair [[p:Rabi Lamichhane]] again questioned journalists' arrests and the police chief's removal.

President [[p:Anura Kumara Dissanayake]], who is also finance minister, presented the 2027 budget. It projects revenue of Rs4.99tn against spending of Rs7.19tn, raises income-tax thresholds, abolishes the tourism levy from April and keeps a 2.3% of GDP primary surplus. The [[p:International Monetary Fund|IMF]] programme expires in March 2027. The second-reading vote is on 20 Nov.
PM [[p:Tarique Rahman]] returned from the [[e:2026 United Nations Climate Change Conference|COP31]] climate conference in Antalya, where he pressed for climate finance; no agreements were announced.
